summary: All six alleged compromise signals were rejected by the Critic; no malicious activity confirmed for prof.kaya@aegean.edu. F4: most successful sign-ins originate from Portugal via university VPN vpn-edge-02 on managed device LT-3104, consistent with expected travel. Remaining events are non-interactive ExchangeSync/15 mail-sync tokens or shared NAT egress, not user logins. Verdict: benign (confidence 0.85).

Exclude ExchangeSync/15 non-interactive mail-sync tokens from impossible-travel and geo-anomaly detections.

Verify vpn-edge-01/02 firmware patches for listed CISA KEV CVEs and monitor appliance exposure independently of this account.

risk.rationale: The only verified account-level signal is F4: most sign-ins originate from Portugal at low likelihood, and the associated sign-ins are through university VPN vpn-edge-02 from managed device LT-3104. The potential account-takeover indicators are rejected/explained: the Turkey and zero-MFA rows are non-interactive ExchangeSync/15 mail-sync tokens, not interactive sign-ins or session replay; 193.140.10.21/Turkcell is shared organizational egress with 202 distinct accounts MFA-ing in 30 days, not a user-specific spray or new network; VPN KEV concerns are mitigated by patched firmware on vpn-edge-02 and no sign-in for this account on vpn-edge-01. No confirmed takeover chain remains.
